answer: A sequential delay gate gives each new identity weight only after it finishes a computation that cannot be split across machines: the run takes one hour of wall-clock time, one step at a time, and the finished output passes through a prism that splits the proof into three separately verified parts. Each part carries a cipher only the identity's own key can decode, proving one machine did the whole run in order. A failed part spirals the audit one epoch further back through past work, so 100 fakes cost 100 separate hours.
